display_name: The whole Wages Protection Act 1983 (NZ) under one top-level goal — for this payment of wages, were the deductions lawful, were the wages paid in a lawful manner, did the employer contravene the Act, and what may be recovered under s 11 — and four goals: deductions and overpayments, the manner of payment, recovery, premiums and penalties

others: the employer may recover the overpayment under s 6 (wpa-deductions.l4)
the wages were paid in a lawful manner (wpa-payment.l4)
the arrears recoverable under s 11A by … on (wpa-enforcement.l4)
liable to a penalty under s 13 (wpa-enforcement.l4)

scope: Every provision of the Act as printed in the PCO's version 25 as at 27 November 2025 (ss 1-19 and the Schedule). Inputs: who is a worker, employer, or person involved (ERA ss 5, 6, 142W); lawful purpose, unreasonableness, duress, consultation; authority under another Act, a collective agreement, an order or a pre-1964 contract; working days for s 6(3)(ba); practicability of acting on a withdrawal. Carried as text: the provisions listed in `provisions carried as text`. NOT encoded: nothing in the Act; the pre-2016 text of the sections the 2016 Act changed is refused.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-15 (tests-independent.l4, 144 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read). It found one error — a s 6 deduction larger than the overpayment counted as lawful in full (s 6(2)) — now fixed (fork F11), and a missing 2016 date gate on s 11A(3), now added. 144/144 now pass. The source text was extracted from the PCO PDF; the PDF is not deposited. The pipeline has not been run. On 2026-10-17, at the user's direction, Legislation Act 2019 s 55 was applied to the employer's 2 weeks to act on a withdrawal of consent or a request (ss 5(2), 9(2)) and the last day for notice of an overpayment (s 6(3)(c)); 4 independent assertion(s) written before that change now fail by design.

forks.F1: ss 5(2), 9(2): a withdrawn consent covers acts up to and including the employer's last day to act on the notice.
forks.F2: s 6(3)(b): notice on the day of recovery is given before recovering.
forks.F3: s 11(1)(a)(iii)-(iv): reach only deductions on or after 27 November 2025.
forks.F4: s 11(1)(a): a s 6 deduction failing s 6(3) is within ground (i).
forks.F5: ss 5(2), 11(1)(a)(i): a deduction after a withdrawal takes effect is within ground (i).
forks.F6: ss 15, 16: deductions under another Act or a collective agreement are not recoverable under s 11.
forks.F7: s 11(2): an action on the sixth anniversary is in time.
forks.F8: s 11(1)(a): a consented deduction for an unlawful purpose is unlawful but outside grounds (i)-(iv).
forks.F9: s 11(1)(b): the whole amount paid in an unlawful manner is recoverable.
forks.F10: Schedule cl 2: conduct before 1 April 2016 is refused, except a s 11 action already out of time (0).
forks.F11: s 6(2): a s 6 deduction is lawful only up to the overpayment.
forks.S55: Legislation Act 2019 s 55 (applied 2026-10-17 at the user's direction): the employer's 2 weeks to act on a withdrawal of consent or a request (ss 5(2), 9(2)) and the last day for notice of an overpayment (s 6(3)(c)) run to the next working day (Legislation Act s 13, with the Matariki dates in Schedule 1 of the Te Kāhui o Matariki Public Holiday Act 2022) when they end on a non-working day.
